# Synthetic hostile-media controls

These fixtures are generated by the adjacent Python module. They contain no patient-derived media, downloaded corpora, weights or third-party exploit payloads. The source is distributed under this repository's Apache-2.0 license.

Positive controls are a blank PDF, a two-by-two grayscale TIFF (also used as a tiny WSI sample), a two-by-two native explicit-little-endian DICOM, a short silent PCM WAV and a one-frame raw YUV4MPEG video. There are no clinical images or identifiers. Negative cases truncate these bytes, alter bounded header/metadata bytes with a fixed seed, create cyclic PDF/TIFF directory references, declare oversized geometry or expand a small compressed PDF stream beyond its declared decoded-byte ceiling.

The worker's private fault controls separately exercise a real process abort, wall timeout, CPU exhaustion, failed allocation under an address-space limit, denied filesystem creation, denied socket creation, environment isolation and discarded native output. These controls are selected explicitly by tests, never by input media bytes. They are not decoder accuracy tests or a substitute for an OS sandbox, fuzzing service or malware scanner.

Run `python -m pytest tests/integration/multimodal/test_hostile_media.py -q`. Native worker cases require 64-bit Linux and working seccomp/resource-limit support. Unsupported hosts exercise the refusal path and explicitly skip native worker cases. Missing optional decoder packages produce `backend_unavailable`; set `OPENMED_REQUIRE_DECODER_BACKENDS=1` in a qualification environment to require all positive controls to decode. The development Linux qualification used Pillow, pydicom/NumPy, pikepdf and PyAV installed separately in a disposable environment; none of their wheels or generated media are committed here.
